title: Theo and the Crown
premise: Tamsin Ravensworth, a mercenary who once swore his blade to the god Vael and now sells outlawed charms to survive, discovers that the old gods have begun answering prayers again after twelve years of silence. Hunted by the Crown's witch-finders, he must reach the Door of Thirteen Turns — the last exit from a country whose borders were erased by conquest — before the moon completes its thirteenth cycle, when the door seals forever and the gods' returning voices demand their debts. Along the way he gathers other debtors of silent gods, learns his own oath was never broken but merely deferred, and must choose between paying Vael's price (his name, his memory, his self) or refusing and dooming everyone who prayed alongside him. In the end Tamsin pays only part of himself — surrendering the mercenary he was — walks through the door as someone new, and leaves the country's survivors a godless but free dawn.
about_author: Juniper Underhill is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing abandoned parish records in northern England, where every empty church felt like a held breath. They write fantasy about faith, debt, and the small stubborn people history forgets.

chapters.title: Charms for a Godless City
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. In the occupied city of Corvane, Tamsin sells minor charms under the nose of Crown witch-finders, hiding the faded brand of his old oath to Vael. A child's prayer he sold a charm for is suddenly, impossibly answered. Emotional beat: dread cracking open into terrified hope — the silence has ended, and he is marked.

chapters.title: The First Answer
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The answered prayer draws witch-finders to his stall; Tamsin flees with help from Odile, a disgraced priestess of a different silent god. He hears Vael's voice for the first time in twelve years: 'The door opens on the thirteenth turn.' Emotional beat: vertigo — the god he mourned is awake, and demanding.

chapters.title: Debtors on the Road
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Traveling toward the rumored Door of Thirteen Turns, they gather others the gods have woken: Brannoc, a soldier sworn to a war-god; Sefa, a girl whose prayer resurrected her brother wrongly. Emotional beat: wary found-family forming among people bound by unpaid vows.

chapters.title: What the Crown Remembers
chapters.summary: Witch-Finder Captain Hale's POV. Hale interrogates prisoners and pieces together that the gods' return coincides with the annexation that erased Tamsin's homeland — the Crown didn't conquer a country; it imprisoned one. Emotional beat: Hale's certainty curdling into complicit horror.

chapters.title: The Country That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The party crosses into land no map acknowledges, where erased villages flicker at dusk and the dead still queue at shuttered shrines. Vael shows Tamsin visions of what his oath originally purchased. Emotional beat: grief — survival itself was the debt, and it has come due.

chapters.title: Sefa's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa attempts to un-resurrect her brother at a flickering shrine; the rite half-succeeds, revealing that the gods can be bargained with — but never refused outright. Brannoc is wounded shielding them from Crown outriders. Emotional beat: desperate agency — there are loopholes, if you're willing to bleed for them.

chapters.title: Hale's Conversion
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Ordered to burn the flicker-villages, Hale instead lets refugees go and defects, bringing the Crown's map of the Door as penance. He confronts Tamsin, whom he's hunted for years. Emotional beat: an enemy kneeling — the hunter asking to become a debtor too.

chapters.title: The Twelfth Turn
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. At the Door of Thirteen Turns, the party finds it guarded by the gods themselves, who offer terms: one full payment — a whole self — or the door seals with everyone inside the erased country forever. Odile volunteers; Tamsin refuses to let her. Emotional beat: love weaponized against sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Climax, Tamsin's POV. As the thirteenth turn begins, Tamsin negotiates with Vael directly, offering not his whole self but the mercenary he became — twelve years of hardened survival — as partial payment. The gods, moved by the first honest bargain in centuries, accept. Emotional beat: agonizing identity-loss chosen freely, transforming duty into gift.

chapters.title: A Godless Dawn
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The door opens; the survivors walk out into a world where their country exists again on no map but their own memories. Tamsin emerges lighter, unnamed, beginning again. The gods fall quiet — listening now, not silent. Emotional beat: bittersweet belonging — home rebuilt not by gods or crowns, but by the people who walked out together.
